candidates.title: PRT journal aborts crisium when a join bond exceeds the signer's balance: the value-bearing preflight eth_call fails with a non-revert code (-32003 anvil, -32000 geth) and hits assert(failure.code == 3), so the documented insufficient_funds report is never reached and the crash repeats on every relaunch before the older epoch's bond recovery that would refill the account
candidates.component: PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes: prt-transactions.lua methods:submit (via prt-bridge.lua methods:attempt for joinTournament, run by crisium.lua pass)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'), standing in for the honest operator (an implementation of an operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-transactions.lua submit lines 218-221 (simulate, then assert(failure.code == 3, "transaction preflight RPC failure")), versus the balance check at lines 254-265 that returns { blocked = "insufficient_funds" }; prt-bridge.lua prepare joinTournament (value = tostring(context.bond)) lines 464-466 and attempt line 653; crisium.lua pass lines 303-314 (newest sealed epoch ticks first) and the main loop (no pcall, any error ends the process; prt-supervise.sh relaunches)
candidates.description: submit() preflights every job with chain:simulate(signer, to, data, value) (eth_call with from and value, no gas price) and treats any failure whose code is not 3 as fatal. An eth_call whose value exceeds the sender's balance is not an EVM revert: anvil answers {code:-32003, 'Insufficient funds for gas * price + value'} and geth fails ApplyMessage with ErrInsufficientFunds, answered with code -32000. The only value-bearing job is joinTournament, which sends the tournament's bond (root and every inner tournament). So whenever the signer's balance is below a bond, submit raises 'transaction preflight RPC failure' instead of returning the graceful { blocked = "insufficient_funds" } that it computes a few lines later (needed = gas*max_fee + value), which report_blocked turns into the documented insufficient_funds anomaly (prt-lua-bridge.md: 'The account cannot pay a transaction's gas at its fee cap'; bridge: 'Reports a transaction the player cannot publish ... Observing continues.'). The graceful branch is reachable only when value <= balance < value + gas*fee. The error propagates out of tick and pass, crisium exits, and every relaunch repeats it at the same place, because crisium ticks the newest sealed epoch first (its root or child join) and only then the older epochs, whose jobs include tryRecoveringBond, the transaction that would return the locked bond and cure the shortfall. Every other job of every epoch (moves with deadlines, gas-only, which the balance can still pay) is starved too.
candidates.trigger: The honest operator's signer holds less than one bond when a join is due. Concrete steady-state scenario: the account holds one bond plus gas. Epoch N's bond stays locked in its finished root tournament until tryRecoveringBond; epoch N+1 is sealed (DaveConsensus seals N+1 when N's result is accepted), and its root join is due. With the designed behaviour, N+1's join is blocked and reported, N's recovery is published in the same pass, and the join succeeds on the next pass. With the defect, the N+1 join's preflight aborts the process before N's recovery is ever attempted, on every relaunch, so the honest claim never joins epoch N+1. Child joins have the same shape: a Sybil population that pairs the honest claim into several concurrent inner tournaments locks one bond per child, and the first child join the balance cannot cover kills the process and with it every other live match. A tip reorg is not needed. Who controls it: the operator's funding (trusted resource), possibly drained by adversary-forced matches if Dave's partial refunds do not cover the honest gas (not checked).
candidates.reachability: Reachable on the honest operator's normal path whenever balance < bond at a join; no adversary data needed. Confirmed on anvil 1.5.1 with the unmodified prt-transactions.lua (see evidence). geth behaviour inferred from its state-transition balance check (value included even with zero gas price) and DoCall returning that error directly.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is the operator's own balance, a provisioned resource; section 4 says 'A host fault, such as a full disk ..., may stop the honest operator'. But the defect is not the stop itself: the code documents insufficient funds as a recoverable, reported condition, and the crash converts a shortfall that its own pending bond recovery would cure into a permanent crash loop that also abandons fundable moves of other matches and epochs. So not excluded on the preferred reading; under the reading that any funding shortfall is an unprovisioned resource, it is Out of scope / Low. 2. Role: prt-transactions.lua and prt-bridge.lua are 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes' = Support; they stand in for the honest operator. Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. 3. High/Medium cases: none of the High cases fits (not data from other parties, not a verifier). 4. Critical in the stood-in role: R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks. After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim' and 'The honest operator defends every epoch whose dispute is open'; the honest claim never joins epoch N+1 (any claim can then win, the goal of section 1 fails) and every other match stalls. Stand-in Critical, so Support caps it at Medium. 5. Alternative: Low as 'a real defect that violates no rule' if insufficient funds are read as an unprovisioned host resource.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support standing in for a Critical R4 violation of the honest operator) / Low (if a balance below one bond is an unprovisioned resource that may stop the operator)
candidates.threat_to_goal: An honest operator funded for its steady state (one bond locked per open epoch plus gas) stops for good at the first epoch transition where the next join precedes the previous recovery, so it never joins the new epoch's root tournament (nor defends anything else); a dishonest claim then wins the epoch unopposed and settles a state the transition function does not define.
candidates.evidence: Scratch script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r5/INVBRIDGE/funds.lua drives the real prt-transactions.lua submit against a fresh anvil (port 18757, stopped afterwards) with a signer stub at an unfunded address and a joinTournament-like intent of value 1 ETH. Result: 'raised: prt-transactions.lua:220: transaction preflight RPC failure'. With the balance set to 1 ETH + 1 wei (value <= balance < value + gas*fee) the same call returns 'graceful: insufficient_funds 1000126000000000000 1000000000000000001'. Raw anvil answers: eth_call with value > balance -> {code:-32003,'Insufficient funds for gas * price + value'}; eth_call reverting with empty data -> code 3; INVALID opcode / out of gas -> code -32603 (also fatal for submit and for the bridge's proof-simulation assert).
candidates.test_idea: Start anvil, build prt-transactions with a fresh journal, a signer stub whose sign() errors, and an intent with value greater than the signer balance (e.g. the root bondValue of a deployed tournament, or any value). Required behaviour (bridge contract: report and keep observing): submit returns a result with blocked = 'insufficient_funds' (or another non-raising blocked/rejected result) and does not raise. The test exits 1 when pcall(submit) raises. A second assertion can drive two bridges (newest epoch first) and check the older epoch's tryRecoveringBond is still published in the same pass.

candidates.title: PRT journal aborts crisium when the 'latest' block it pinned is reorged out before its blockHash-pinned nonce or preflight call (-32001 'Resource not found' / 'not canonical'), while the bridge's own proof preflight checks canonicity before asserting
candidates.component: PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes: prt-transactions.lua methods:submit and methods:nonce
candidates.role: Support (PRT player and bridge), standing in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-transactions.lua submit lines 161-163 (block = latest; nonce(address, { blockHash = block.hash, requireCanonical = true }) -> methods:nonce line 36 eth.small(assert(count, ...))) and lines 218-221 (simulate at { blockHash = block.hash, requireCanonical = true }, then assert(failure.code == 3)); contrast prt-bridge.lua attempt lines 621-631, which returns nil when the head is no longer canonical before asserting on the failure code
candidates.description: submit reads the latest block, then issues several RPCs pinned to that block's hash with requireCanonical = true (the nonce, then after receipt, fee and transaction queries, the preflight eth_call). If a one-block reorg replaces that tip in between, the node answers with an error that is not an EVM revert (anvil -32001 'Resource not found'; geth -32000 'hash is not currently canonical' / header not found). methods:nonce asserts on any error and submit asserts failure.code == 3, so the whole crisium process exits. The comment in submit ('A changed branch may need immediate republication') and the bridge's attempt() (which re-checks is_canonical before its own code-3 assert) show tip reorgs are meant to be tolerated, so this is an unguarded path rather than a design choice. The process is relaunched by prt-supervise.sh, so the cost is a restart (reopen every kept epoch, rehash machines) at the moment a deadline-bound transaction was being submitted.
candidates.trigger: Chain behaviour: a reorg of the tip block during the few RPC round trips of one submit. Not controlled by an adversary (the model does not grant reorgs), but ordinary on PoS L1 (single-slot reorgs) and possible on L2 sequencers.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on every submit, with a small race window per submission; demonstrated at the RPC level on anvil (anvil_reorg 1, then eth_getTransactionCount and eth_call with the orphaned blockHash and requireCanonical=true both return code -32001).
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Section 4: 'Acting on history before it is final, and recovering when that history is replaced, is outside this model.' The journal deliberately acts at the tip (inclusion), and the dispute observation is pre-finality, so a strict reading puts recovery from a tip reorg out of scope. Preferred reading: the reorg does not change the history the operator acted on (it only invalidates a block hash used as a read pin), so the crash is a plain robustness defect. 2. Role: Support (PRT player and bridge), standing in for the honest operator. 3. High/Medium cases: none fits directly. 4. Critical in the stood-in role only if a crash-restart at a submission can push an honest response past its deadline (R4 'submits its transactions within the dispute clocks'); a single restart is bounded, so this is weak. 5. Low: a robustness defect that violates no rule once restarts are absorbed by the clocks.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (preferred) / Medium (if a restart forced at submission time is read as threatening R4 timeliness in the stood-in honest role) / Out of scope (strict pre-finality reading)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Each occurrence costs a full relaunch of the player exactly when it was publishing a (possibly deadline-bound) move; on its own it does not break the goal, but it removes margin from the clocks the honest operator relies on.
candidates.evidence: anvil 1.5.1 on a scratch port: after anvil_mine 5 and anvil_reorg 1, eth_getTransactionCount and eth_call with params {blockHash: <old tip>, requireCanonical: true} return {code:-32001,'Resource not found'}. By reading: methods:nonce (line 35-36) asserts on any RPC error; submit line 220 asserts failure.code == 3.
candidates.test_idea: Mock chain object for prt-transactions whose rpc('eth_getTransactionCount', {addr, {blockHash=...}}) and simulate(...) return nil, {code=-32001} (as a reorged pin does), while is_canonical(block) returns false. Required: submit returns a non-raising result (e.g. { waiting = true }) so the tick retries at the new tip. Test exits 1 when pcall(submit) raises.

candidates.title: cartesi-machine CLI aborts --mcycle-computation-hash / --uarch-cycle-computation-hash runs at the first accepted input whose outputs Merkle root differs from the CLI's own outputs frontier (check_outputs_merkle_root defaults to true), so no claim is computed for an application that breaks the outputs-root convention
candidates.component: cartesi-machine CLI (src/cartesi-machine.lua), cmio advance-state driver used by its computation-hash options
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'the cartesi-machine CLI ... Support'); stands in for a tool that computes claims
candidates.location: src/cartesi-machine.lua flush_pending_outputs lines 3691-3697 (assertf(frontier root == data, 'outputs Merkle root mismatch at input %d')), default set at line 2084 (check_outputs_merkle_root = true), called from run_advance_state_input line 3723 before builder:end_input; the computation hash (report_computation_hash via end_epoch) is never reached
candidates.description: Variant site of the pending R4-RGPLAYERGUEST-1 (which is the length check at line 3689 of the same function). With the default check_outputs_merkle_root:true, an accepted input whose tx-buffer root (32 bytes, so the length check passes) differs from the keccak frontier of the outputs the guest emitted aborts the whole run with an assert. Computing the claim depends only on state hashes, and the PRT stored player reports the same condition as the outputs_merkle_root_mismatch anomaly and continues, whereas the CLI stops. Guest-controlled: any application that accepts with a stale or differently built root (not correctly designed) triggers it.
candidates.trigger: Guest code after it reads an input: emits outputs and then accepts with a 32-byte root that is not the frontier root (or emits none and writes any other 32 bytes).
candidates.reachability: Any guest can reach it (guest-writable tx buffer and yield data are presumed reachable). Read only; not run.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Section 8: an application that breaks the rollup interface 'must never stop the honest operator from computing claims or producing proofs. Development tools may instead stop and report the violation.' The CLI is a development tool, so this stop is explicitly allowed unless the CLI is read as the stood-in claim-computing operator tool. 2. Role: Support (CLI). 3. High/Medium cases: if the CLI counts as 'a tool that computes claims' (as triage read it for R1-R6-1), stopping on guest data would be an R4 violation in the honest role ('This holds for every guest, whether or not its application is correctly designed'), Critical there, so Medium for support. 4. n/a. 5. Under the development-tool clause it is Low or Out of scope.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low / Out of scope (development tools may stop and report the violation); Medium only if the CLI is the stood-in claim-computing tool. Likely a duplicate-family of R4-RGPLAYERGUEST-1.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None for a deployment (no production node runs the CLI); it violates R4's 'every guest' only if the CLI is held to the honest operator's standard.
candidates.test_idea: Bare-metal guest that, at its first input, emits one output and then accepts with 32 zero bytes in the tx buffer; run cartesi-machine with --cmio-advance-state=... and --mcycle-computation-hash=log2_mcycle_period:N; required: the run prints 'Mcycle computation hash:' (or exits 0 with check_outputs_merkle_root reported as a warning); the test exits 1 when the CLI aborts with 'outputs Merkle root mismatch'.
